newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse trade at record levels.
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse trade at record levels.

text.p: German equities ended bourse trade at a record high on Friday, but failed to penetrate the 2,800-point level -- a psychologically-important threshold for the blue chip DAX index.
The DAX index closed at 2,795.80 points, up 18.79 points or 0.68 percent. The index index had reached an intraday high of 2,799.05 points, tantalisingly close to the 2,800-point mark.
Share trade was underpinned by a record close on Wall Street overnight and the strength of the dollar.

"This is very good, coming just before the Telekom flotation on Monday. The market is favouring different sectors in turn -- chemicals, utilities, cars and now the banks. This is a very healthy bull market," a Frankfurt trader said.

The three biggest German banks were among the heaviest-traded stocks in Frankfurt over the course of bourse trade as traders focused on banks amid speculation about mergers and takeovers within the sector.

Commerzbank AG started bourse trade higher, but the price was hit by profit-taking over the session and it ended down five pfennigs at 36.60 marks. Nearly three million Commerzbank shares changed hands over floor trade.
Dresdner Bank AG ended up 30 pfennigs at 44.70 marks, while Deutsche Bank AG ended up 15 pfennigs at 72.35 marks.
Electronics group Siemens AG was among the session losers, ending down 26 pfennigs at 73.64 marks.
Dealers said the group was suffering after profit warnings in its passive components and electron tubes division on Thursday and the generally poor outlook for the German electronics sector.
